findings.title: C4_root_winsor rewrites away a cs_winsor that is not rank-neutral, and the two spellings share a dedup_key
findings.summary: `root: cs_winsor(_) -> operand` is declared as an equivalence-preserving rewrite, but the 1%/99% clip is re-estimated every day and the reward's causal EMA mixes days, so ema(clip(x)) is not a monotone map of ema(x); `canonical()` and `dedup_key()` nevertheless treat `cs_winsor(X)` and `X` as the same experiment.
findings.failure_scenario: Input: F112's own corpus pair (runs/F112_scale_spow_masktop/sweep_s3.json). v_base = `ts_scale(signedpower(cs_mask_top_replace_mean_neg(add(day_quantile(Close), day_kurt(High)))), 30)` scores utrain long_sharpe 0.74, train long_ann 0.037, valid long_ann 0.053. The `win` variant `cs_winsor(<same tree>)` scores utrain long_sharpe -0.25, train long_ann -0.021, valid long_ann 0.012, with corr_orig 0.826 (B01.yaml claims rho ~0.99). Both have hl_long_u = 20, so the difference is purely the clip. `G.canonical(win) == G.canonical(v_base)` and `G.dedup_key(win) == G.dedup_key(v_base)` are both True, so in scripts/idea_search.py:222 whichever spelling is proposed first wins and the other returns False as `equivalent` -> the reported number for one is attributed to the other, wrong by 0.99 utrain Sharpe and by a sign flip in train long_ann. Same root cause makes `cs_winsor` non-idempotent (steer.py:171): on a heavy-tailed cross-section max |cs_winsor(cs_winsor(x)) - cs_winsor(x)| = 7.66 (relative 5.6e-3) because torch.nanquantile interpolates linearly and the clipped tail moves the 99% point; `simplify()` collapses it anyway. `cs_robust_z` in the same list is off by a relative 1e9 on a near-constant cross-section (EPS in the denominator).
findings.evidence: Repro: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/matcher-guidance/probe5.py (C4 table over all 15 factors: median |d utrain Sharpe| = 0.02 but F112 = -0.99, F110 = +0.31; corr_orig 0.826 / 0.95) and /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/matcher-guidance/probe7.py (idempotency by input family; `canonical('cs_winsor(cs_winsor(day_std(Amt)))') == 'day_std(Amt)'`). Mechanism is stated in /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/ops_ext.py:253 cs_winsor's own docstring ("the EMA of a raw heavy-tailed value is a peak memory, the EMA of the clipped value is a level").
findings.suggested_fix: Demote C4 from `rewrite` to `weight` (or gate it on hl == 0), since the evidence behind it is a median over 15 seeds, not a pointwise identity. Drop `cs_winsor` and `cs_robust_z` from IDEMPOTENT_OPS in /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/steer.py:171, or add a guard that only collapses when the rewrite is also applied to the smoothed panel.

findings.title: operator_weights() silently drops the `root:` anchor, so root-only bans become global operator bans in the steer arm
findings.summary: `operator_weights()` keys on `r.pattern.tree.name` without checking `r.pattern.root`, so B1/B2 (root-only bans) emit a 0.0 multiplier and D2/D3/D13 (root-only down-weights) emit a global one; meanwhile 5 of the 7 up-weight rules are skipped because their patterns carry a non-generic arg. scripts/idea_search.py:200 removes any 0.0-weight operator from the sampling vocabulary entirely.
findings.failure_scenario: Input: `Guidance.load('guidance/B01.yaml').operator_weights()` returns {'cross_zscore': 0.0, 'ts_zscore': 0.0, 'cs_mean': 0.0, 'cs_sum': 0.0, 'cs_median': 0.0, 'cs_stddev_full': 0.0, 'cs_max': 0.0, 'cs_min': 0.0, 'ts_product': 0.0, 'cross_stddev': 0.3, 'ts_stddev': 0.3, 'cross_min': 0.5, 'ts_min': 0.5, 'div': 0.5, 'cross_sum': 0.5, 'ts_sum': 0.5, 'ts_scale': 0.5, 'cs_rank': 0.6, 'cs_bucket_*': 2.0, 'cs_last_high*': 1.5}. B2 (B01.yaml:100) bans the cs_* day scalars only at the ROOT, but in scripts/idea_search.py:199-200 `w *= OPW.get(s.name, 1.0)` then `if w > 0` means the steer arm can never place `cs_mean`/`cs_median`/`cs_stddev_full`/`cs_sum`/`cross_zscore`/`ts_product` anywhere in a tree. 12 of the corpus's 408 good candidates use a cs_* day scalar non-root and are therefore unreachable: F102 h_ov_state (utrain long_sharpe 2.59), F114 h_gate_vol_mix (2.58, valid long_ann 0.241), F114 h_gate_disp_mix (2.52), F108 h_gate_lowvol (2.26), F101 h_rv_fold_state_weight (2.25). Root-only D13 becomes a global 0.6 on cs_rank, which appears non-root 347 times in the corpus; root-only D2 becomes a global 0.3 on cross_stddev. In the other direction U1/U2/U3/U6/U7 contribute nothing (their args `{30|60}` / `{Ret|@price}` / nested sub-trees fail the `generic` test at steer.py:334), so the table the steer arm actually receives is a one-sided penalty list -> the E6 steer-vs-control episode numbers measure a vocabulary restriction, not the guidance the file states.
findings.evidence: Repro: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/matcher-guidance/repro.py section F1 (prints the OPW dict, the `root=True` flags of B1/B2/D2/D3/D13, the 12 good non-root cs_* candidates and the 347 non-root cs_rank uses). Consumer: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/scripts/idea_search.py:182, 199, 200.
findings.suggested_fix: In `operator_weights()` skip any rule with `r.pattern.root` (same treatment it already gives `unless` / `depth_ge`), or emit root-anchored rules on a separate channel. Independently, have idea_search floor the multiplier at a small epsilon instead of dropping zero-weight operators, so a context-specific ban cannot silently delete an operator from the grammar.

findings.title: dedup_key collapses every price leaf globally, merging expressions that are not the same experiment
findings.summary: C7's leaf-family collapse is applied as a global regex substitution over the whole canonical string, so an expression containing two or more DIFFERENT price leaves is merged with structurally different expressions; in idea_search the loser of a bucket is rejected as `equivalent` and can never be scored in that run.
findings.failure_scenario: Input: `G.dedup_key('sub(High, Low)')`, `G.dedup_key('sub(Close, Open)')` and `G.dedup_key('sub(High, Close)')` all return `sub(Close,Close)` - the daily range, the daily return and the upper shadow become one experiment whose representative is identically 0. `div(sub(Close, Low), sub(High, Low))` (position in the day's range, bounded [0,1]) and `div(sub(High, Close), sub(High, Low))` both return `div(sub(Close,Close),sub(Close,Close))`, i.e. 0/0. In /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/scripts/idea_search.py:221-224, `first_form.setdefault(key, e) != e` -> `return False` with `stats['equivalent'] += 1`, so once any member of such a bucket is proposed, every other member is dropped unscored for the rest of the run. Already live on the corpus: 4 dedup buckets hold more than one distinct canonical form with up to 1.07 utrain long_sharpe spread - e.g. F109 `fld_Close_Low` (-0.57) / `leaf_Close_low` (-1.04) / `fld_Close_High` (-1.38), and F112 `v_base` (0.74, `add(day_quantile(Close), day_kurt(High))`) merged with `leaf_High_close` (0.79, `add(day_quantile(Close), day_kurt(Close))`). C7's evidence is a single-leaf swap in an otherwise identical tree (rho 0.96-0.98); it does not license a per-occurrence substitution.
findings.evidence: Repro: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/matcher-guidance/repro.py section F3 (prints the merged buckets for the range family and the 4 live corpus buckets with their utrain-Sharpe spreads).
findings.suggested_fix: Only apply the leaf collapse when the canonical form contains at most one distinct price leaf (or collapse per leaf-position rather than per name, e.g. rename the FIRST distinct price leaf to Close, the second to Close2, ...), and refuse to collapse when the substitution would make any `sub`/`div` have two identical operands.

findings.title: B3_day_scalar_multiplier is an unconditional ban, but its no-op argument only holds when the day-scalar multiply is the last op before the cross-sectional rank
findings.summary: The ban removes `{mul|div}(_, cs_<scalar>(_))` anywhere in the tree with weight 0; 3 of its 7 corpus hits (43% vs a 14.4% base rate) are candidates that clear the selection bar, including the best valid-period long leg in the F114 family.
findings.failure_scenario: Input: the three good hits are banned outright (`G.banned(expr) == True`, weight 0, so `accept()` always returns False). F114 h_gate_vol_mix `add(cs_rank(cross_mean(day_std(Amt), 30)), mul(cs_rank(cross_ema(cross_quantile_q25(day_close(Ret), 60), 30)), cs_mean(div(cross_mean(day_sum(Amt), 5), cross_mean(day_sum(Amt), 60)))))` has utrain long_sharpe 2.58, train long_ann 0.140, valid long_ann 0.241; F108 h_gate_lowvol 2.26 / 0.107 / 0.202; F101 h_rv_fold_state_weight 2.25 / 0.103 / 0.065. The `why` ("a day scalar spread across the cross-section is wiped out by the rank") is false in both shapes present here: (a) inside `add(cs_rank(known), mul(cs_rank(X), scalar))` the day scalar re-weights the two legs and so changes that day's cross-section; (b) the reward smooths with a causal EMA before ranking (partura/steer.py:426 -> books.smoothed -> alphacube.metrics.ema_rows), so a per-day scale changes which days dominate the smoothed signal - exactly what those variants' own `why` text says they are testing. The pattern is also order-asymmetric and escapes through one wrapper: `mul(cs_rank(day_std(Amt)), cs_mean(day_std(Ret)))` is banned while `mul(cs_mean(day_std(Ret)), cs_rank(day_std(Amt)))` and `mul(cs_rank(day_std(Amt)), inv(cs_mean(day_std(Ret))))` are not (F112 h_state_thin uses the `inv` form and escapes).
findings.evidence: Repro: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/matcher-guidance/repro.py section F2 (7 hits with good/bad labels and their utrain/train/valid numbers, plus the three order/wrapper probes). Corpus: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/runs/F114_q25_closeret/sweep_s3.json key `h_gate_vol_mix`.
findings.suggested_fix: Anchor the rule to the case it is about - `root: {mul|div}(_, {cs_mean|...}(_))` with an `unless` for being inside an `add`, or drop it from `ban` to a `weight` - and make it order-insensitive (match the day scalar in either operand of `mul`).

findings.title: B4_abs_epsilon_denominator bans any additive constant denominator, anywhere in the tree, and kills the only F109 variants that beat the known family
findings.summary: `$w` matches any number, not just an epsilon, and the pattern is not root-anchored, so the ban propagates from a spine into every blend/screen built on top of it.
findings.failure_scenario: Input: `G.banned('div(Amt, add(day_std(Amt), create_like(Amt, 1)))')` returns True although the `why` is explicitly about +1e-6; `$w` in the pattern accepts 1, 5 or any other scale-setting constant. Because the pattern is not `root:`-anchored, the ban also fires on 388 of the 2839 corpus variants, 7 of which clear the selection bar - including the two best results in the whole F109 family: h3_blend_tailq75 (utrain long_sharpe 2.50, train long_ann 0.147, valid long_ann 0.226) and h3_fam_x_tailq75 (2.49 / 0.141 / 0.230), plus scr_xhi_p (2.37 / 0.129 / 0.224). Those are precisely the variants that beat the known family's 2.22, and they are unreachable under the guidance because the epsilon sits deep inside the spine they screen/blend with, not at the root where the ablation evidence was collected.
findings.evidence: Repro: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/matcher-guidance/repro.py section F4 (388 hits, 7 good, the top three listed with numbers, and the plain +1 probe). Corpus: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/runs/F109_erm_mag_gap_5m_tsm20/sweep_s3.json keys `h3_blend_tailq75`, `h3_fam_x_tailq75`.
findings.suggested_fix: Tighten `$w` to a magnitude range (e.g. a dedicated `$eps` token, or `|w| < 1e-3`), and either anchor the rule so it only bans the epsilon in the candidate's own newly generated sub-tree, or exempt matches that lie inside a known-pool spine (an `unless` on `cs_last_high20(...)` / `add(cs_rank(cross_mean(day_std(Amt), 30)), _)`).

findings.title: nesting() counts non-adjacent occurrences and dies on alternation heads, so depth_ge rules fire on structures their `why` does not describe
findings.summary: `nesting` returns the maximum NUMBER of nodes with that name along any root-to-leaf path, not the deepest adjacent chain; and `Rule.hits` calls it with `self.pattern.tree.name`, which for a `{a|b}` head is the literal brace string, so such a rule can never fire. Two more silent no-ops sit beside it: C3's `to: single_power` is unimplemented, and `{a|b}` compares numeric arguments by text while a bare literal compares them numerically.
findings.failure_scenario: (a) D15_ema_of_ema (B01.yaml:119, w=0.2, `why` = "memory wrapping memory") hits `cross_ema(day_std(cross_ema(Amt, 5)), 30)` - a daily statistic OF a smoothed panel, then smoothed, which is not the double-wrapping the rule was written for. D11_nested_rolling_max (B01.yaml:115, w=0.2, `why` = "three or more nested rolling maxima") hits `ts_max(cross_mean(ts_max(cross_mean(ts_max(Amt,5),3),5),7),9)` where no two ts_max are adjacent; it down-weights 207 of the 2839 corpus variants by 5x. (b) A rule written as `{cross_ema|cross_mean}(_, $w)` with `depth_ge: 2` never fires: `nesting(n, '{cross_ema|cross_mean}')` is 0, so `hits()` is always False - any future consolidation of D15/D16 into one alternation rule silently disables it. (c) `Pattern._name_ok` (steer.py:128) does a string compare inside braces while `_match` (steer.py:146) does `float(n.name) == float(p.name)` for a bare literal: `cross_mean(Amt, 30.0)` matches `cross_mean(_, 30)` but NOT `cross_mean(_, {30|60})`, so U1/U3/U7/D6's window lists stop matching the moment a generator prints a float window. (d) `Guidance._apply` (steer.py:261) returns the node unchanged for `to: single_power`, so C3_nested_powers is a dead rule: `canonical('pow_2(pow_2(day_std(Amt))))')` returns the input, and `pow_1_5(pow_2(x))` keeps a different dedup_key from `pow_3(x)` so both get evaluated. Implementing it naively would be unsound: `sqrt(pow_3(x))` = |x|^1.5 for x<0 but `pow_1_5(x)` = NaN. (e) Dead names: `neg_abs` (IDEMPOTENT_OPS), `ts_zscore` (B1), `cs_max`/`cs_min` (B2) do not exist in the 304-name operator catalog; `in_slice` is in SIGN_KEEPING_OPS but is not a catalog operator.
findings.evidence: Repro: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/matcher-guidance/repro.py sections F5 and F6 (nesting counts, D15/D11 hits, the brace-head depth_ge probe, the three C3 canonical calls, the 30 vs 30.0 vs +30 table, and the catalog-membership check against alphacube.catalog.default_registry()).
findings.suggested_fix: Make `nesting` count only adjacent chains (`here + max(child_chain)` where `here` resets the child count to 0 when the child's name differs), or rename it and give `depth_ge` an explicit "count on a path" semantic in the file header. In `Rule.hits`, expand an alternation head and take the max nesting over its names. Make `_name_ok` compare numerically when both sides parse as numbers. Either implement `single_power` with a nonneg guard on the inner operand or delete C3. Remove `neg_abs`, `ts_zscore`, `cs_max`, `cs_min`, and add a startup assertion that every name in the three lists and in every pattern exists in the catalog.

checked_and_fine: parse_expr reads the AlphaCube repr correctly: negative constants (`mul(Close, -1)`, `-5`, `-1.0`, `-0.25`), scientific notation (`1e-06`, `1E-06`, `-1.5e-3`), leading `+` (`+30`), and operator names with underscores and digits (`nt_ts_autocorr_s1`, `pow_1_5`, `cross_quantile_q25`, `in_slice_to_end`, `cs_last_high20`). All 2839 real expressions in /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/runs/F1*/sweep_s3.json parse, and `Guidance.canonical` runs on all of them without raising. Genuinely malformed input (`mul(Close, - 1)`) raises ValueError as intended, and idea_search treats that as `unread` rather than judging the tree.

Every name in NONNEG_OPS verified numerically nonneg on signed input: day_std, day_var, day_gini, day_zero_ratio, day_flat_ratio, day_distinct_ratio, day_at_max_ratio, day_at_min_ratio, day_flat_run_max, day_pos_ratio, day_wstd, cross_stddev, ts_stddev, cross_valid_count, cross_age, cross_flat_ratio, cross_semistd_neg, cross_semistd_pos, cs_rank, in_stddev_rolling, in_stddev_full, nt_ts_std, nt_ts_var, abs_, pow_2, sqrt, sigmoid. In particular day_gini takes |x| before the Gini, so `day_gini(Ret)` is nonneg despite a possibly negative daily mean; cs_rank is a pct rank in (0,1]; sqrt is sqrt(|x|); pow_2 = pow_(x, 2.0) with e>1 so it is x^2. Script: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/matcher-guidance/probe6.py.

Every name in SIGN_KEEPING_OPS verified: a nonneg operand gives a nonneg output, including the ones worth doubting - div (x/y with x,y>=0), mul, add, cs_winsor (clips to its own quantiles), signedpower (sign(x)|x|^e), pow_05/pow_1_5/pow_2_5/pow_3, cross_fangzheng (= cross_mean + cross_stddev, both nonneg on nonneg input), day_quantile (torch.nanquantile), cross_tail_mean_q25/q75, cross_quantile_q25/q75, in_delay, in_local_mean, in_mean_full. `nonneg()` also correctly recurses into numeric args, so `mul(Amt, -1)` is not claimed nonneg, and `Ret` (not in @price/@flow) is not claimed nonneg.

abs_, cs_demean, cs_rank and cs_normalize are exactly idempotent (max |f(f(x)) - f(x)| <= 9e-13 across gaussian, heavy-tailed and near-constant cross-sections), so those four entries in IDEMPOTENT_OPS are safe. `simplify`'s guard `len(n.args) == 1` means the collapse never fires on an operator carrying a window or quantile argument, which is conservative in the right direction.

C1_window1_identity, C2_abs_of_nonneg and C5_cov_self are exact rewrites, and the `_1` back-substitution in `Guidance._apply` handles multi-token subtrees correctly (`day_cov(cross_mean(Amt, 30), cross_mean(Amt, 30))` -> `day_var(cross_mean(Amt, 30))`).

C6_shift_scale_const is sound through the whole selection convention, which I checked rather than assumed: alphacube.metrics.ema_rows (/Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube/src/alphacube/metrics.py:215) is an affine recursion whose coefficients sum to 1 and whose state carries across missing days, so EMA(x+c) = EMA(x)+c and EMA(w*x) = w*EMA(x) exactly; the top-decile equal-weight book is invariant to both. A negative w is a pure sign flip, which `reward()` searches over explicitly, so it is equivalent under the convention. The only unsound case is w == 0 (`mul(x, 0)` would be rewritten to a live expression), and no corpus variant has a root-level multiply by 0.

`root:` anchoring is implemented consistently in both matching paths: `Pattern.find` returns only the whole tree, and `Guidance._apply` returns early for a root rule at a non-top node, so a root rewrite never fires mid-tree. D1's `unless` pattern is structurally anchored (`{abs_|pow_2}(cs_demean({day_std|...}(_)))`), so it exempts exactly the intraday-dispersion folds its `why` names and nothing else; I found no corpus case where the globally-evaluated `unless` granted a spurious exemption.

accept()'s thinning is proportional for weight <= w_ref and reproducible both ways (per-draw `u`, or the sha1 of the dedup_key for a fixed list). Measured on the corpus: w_ref = 2.0 (the max single rule weight), 699/2839 rule-free variants are therefore accepted with probability 0.5, and 135/2839 whose rule product exceeds 2.0 (observed up to 6.0) are clipped to probability 1 - so the ordering among the strongly up-weighted candidates is not delivered. This is stated in the docstring ("capped at w_ref") rather than a bug, but if the intent is to deliver the full product, w_ref should be the max achievable product and the neutral acceptance rate should be reconsidered against the budget cost.
